verified_by_main_session.acceptance_tests: 16 of 17 pass in the worktree; re-run by hand, claim confirmed
verified_by_main_session.what_ac15_asserts: Scans workflowText for every /test[-_ ]?author/gi match (9 in the file) and asserts scoped_diff_ref does not appear within a -500/+1000 CHARACTER window of each. It measures file layout, not behaviour.
verified_by_main_session.is_the_requirement_met: Yes. The real requirement — the Test Author repair prompt carries no scoped_diff_ref — is satisfied. The failure is an unrelated AT("test-author") on one line sitting 347 chars before a scoped_diff_ref literal in a DIFFERENT prompt.

structural_findings: A MUTATING FINDING CHAIN DEFEATS repeat_finding. Three rounds were spent on three variants of the same AC-15 issue, each with a different dedupe_key, so the same-key-twice stop never fired and the round cap expired instead.

THE LOOP ESCALATED ON THE ROUND THAT FIRST RAISED THE OPEN FINDING, with zero fixer attempts on it. shouldEscalate returned max_rounds in the same round the finding appeared, so the last round's findings never get a fix attempt.

isTestFinding() ROUTES BY LOCATION. This finding is about a test assertion but is located at the workflow file, so it went to the code Fixer, whose prompt forbids editing tests under .artifacts/tests/. A finding only fixable by editing a test, routed to an agent forbidden to edit tests, is a deadlock.

options_for_the_human.accept_and_fix_the_test: Recommended. Replace the character-window proxy with an assertion on the actual test-repair prompt string. The implementation is correct; the test asserts layout.
options_for_the_human.contort_the_code: Hoist the prompt construction into a legal line range so the window clears. The packager verified this works, but the windows move as text moves, so it is a change made to satisfy a brittle assertion rather than a contract.
options_for_the_human.drop_the_work_item: Keep the escalation as the finding and leave the fix-loop cost work unshipped.

payload.irony: The work item to make the fix loop cheaper was killed by an expensive fix loop — and the three structural findings above came out of exactly that.
